walkthroughs.body_html:
Inorganic Chemistry — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Inorganic Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Inorganic Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Can you determine the order of a reaction with respect to a reactant from the balanced equation?
options: A coordination number of 4 always means square planar because complexes prefer to be flat.
The order of reaction is always equal to the number of reactants in the equation.
The order of reaction with respect to each reactant equals its coefficient in the balanced equation.
No — orders must be determined experimentally; they often differ from the stoichiometric coefficients.

mcqs.q: If a complex ion has a coordination number of 4, what shape does it have?
options: The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
It can be either tetrahedral OR square planar — the shape depends on the metal and ligands (e.g. [Pt(NH3)4]2+ is square planar; [CuCl4]2- is tetrahedral).
A coordination number of 4 always means square planar because complexes prefer to be flat.
A coordination number of 4 always means tetrahedral, because that gives the maximum bond-angle separation.

mcqs.q: If 50 cm^3 of a 1 mol/dm^3 solution is diluted to 100 cm^3, what is the new concentration?
options: A coordination number of 4 always means square planar because complexes prefer to be flat.
0.5 mol/dm^3 — the moles stay the same but the volume doubled.
The new concentration is 0.05 mol/dm^3 because you doubled the volume so you halve the concentration once and shift the decimal too.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
